comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1, C49, C59-C63. Both evaluations support the identification of Snhg3 through RNA-Seq screening and RT-qPCR validation. OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation while peer reviewers acknowledge this as a strength of the screening strategy.

Perfect agreement on claims C2-C3. Both support the in vitro findings showing PA-induced Snhg3 expression and lipid accumulation with Snhg3 overexpression. Neither evaluation questions these experimental results.

Strong agreement on claims C4-C6, C67, C70-C79 regarding Snhg3-HKO phenotype. Both evaluations appreciate the tissue-specific knockout model development and phenotypic characterization. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of statistical rigor while peer reviewers emphasize the value of generating lncRNA knockout models.

Perfect agreement on claims C7, C80-C87. Both support the complementary knock-in model showing opposite phenotypes. OpenEval emphasizes bidirectional effects strengthening causality while peer reviewers acknowledge the solid evidence backing these studies.

Agreement on claims C89-C90, C92-C93 regarding gene expression changes. Both evaluations support the RNA-Seq and validation approaches. OpenEval covers additional claims (C91) about Scd1/2 function not explicitly mentioned in peer review.

Strong agreement on claims C94-C96, C98-C101 regarding ATAC-Seq and chromatin accessibility. Both acknowledge the unbiased approaches used. OpenEval notes the need for further validation of causal relationships while peer reviewers accept the findings without specific concerns.

Agreement on claims C102-C105 regarding Snhg3-SND1 interaction. Both evaluations support the convergence of mass spectrometry, prediction, and experimental validation. Peer reviewers explicitly note this as a strength using multiple molecular approaches.

Agreement on claims C106-C108, C111-C113 regarding SND1 regulation through ubiquitination and stability. Both support these mechanistic findings. OpenEval provides more detailed assessment of the ubiquitination experiments while peer reviewers acknowledge the solid evidence.

Agreement on claims C121-C124 regarding H3K27me3 regulation by SND1. Both support the mechanistic connection. OpenEval notes the mechanism by which SND1 regulates H3K27me3 is not fully elucidated, while peer reviewers accept the findings without challenge.

Agreement on claims C125-C130 regarding H3K27me3 enrichment at Pparg promoter. Both support the CUT&Tag and ChIP data. OpenEval emphasizes the bidirectional effects while peer reviewers acknowledge the chromatin remodeling mechanism.

Agreement on claims C132-C136 regarding PPAR gamma regulation. Both support the connection between SND1 and PPAR gamma expression. OpenEval emphasizes rescue experiments while peer reviewers acknowledge the regulatory circuit.

Agreement on claims C14, C147-C151 regarding PPAR gamma antagonist validation. Both support the pharmacological intervention data. OpenEval notes unexpected lack of effects on some parameters while peer reviewers accept the evidence without specific concerns.

Perfect agreement on claims C142-C144 regarding U17 snoRNA independence. Both support the control experiments showing effects are due to Snhg3 itself rather than its snoRNA product. Neither evaluation raises concerns about this important control.

Divergent evaluations on claims C17-C18, C58, C200-C203 regarding the overall signaling pathway. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with acknowledgment of partial responsibility, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting the study is incomplete and requires future validation. This represents the main area of disagreement.

Agreement on claims C204-C206 regarding study limitations. Both acknowledge mechanistic gaps, particularly regarding how SND1 regulates H3K27me3. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED (appropriate acknowledgment of limitations) while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, aligning with the editor's comment about incompleteness.

OpenEval evaluated claims C64-C66 regarding Snhg3's non-coding nature and cytoplasmic localization as SUPPORTED based on computational prediction and fractionation experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
